objectives.description: Redeploy via deploy-headless.sh (multiple passes as residual issues were found)
Fix SKILL.md context-budget overage via trim + reviewed ceiling move (precedent convention)
Fix a real shellcheck SC2066 finding in test-gate-contention-tagging.sh
Fix a real unit/integration misclassification for test-batch-gate-pending-marker.sh

Fix a real production-impacting marker-file leak risk in test-batch-gate-pending-marker.sh's Case 7 (real-repo write -> isolated-fixture rewrite), plus the underlying nested-env-inheritance root cause

approaches_tried.approach: Seed a fixed-name batch-gate-pending marker in the REAL repo's specs/.orchestration/ to test run-all.sh's own guard (run-all.sh has no explicit TARGET override)
approaches_tried.reason: A fixed session name collided with a concurrently-running instance of the same suite under a sibling session's own full battery; measured live as 21 accumulated leftover marker files in the real repo, each capable of spuriously deferring an unrelated verify-deploy.sh/run-all.sh invocation elsewhere. A PID-unique filename closed the two-concurrent-instance race but not a SIGKILL-bypassed-trap leak under extreme load. Replaced entirely with an isolated, path-mirrored run-all.sh fixture copy under the suite's own TMPTARGET, eliminating any real-repo interaction.

notes: Measured Gate 8 wall-clock: 349s (5m49s-5m50s), nproc=24, loadavg 4.15 and 7.22 respectively (two independent standalone --only-gate 8 runs) -- under the 600s ceiling with 251s (~42%) headroom, under REAL non-idle load (an idle control was never available this dispatch; see Phase 1's own deferred baseline and this phase's Reasoned Exclusions for why).

Discovered and fixed a genuine, significant bug mid-phase: test-batch-gate-pending-marker.sh's Case 7 wrote a batch-gate-pending marker directly into the REAL repository's specs/.orchestration/ directory (to test run-all.sh's own entry guard, which has no TARGET override). Under this host's sustained multi-session load, this leaked 21 files across one run alone (confirmed via live reproduction and PID-liveness checks) -- each capable of spuriously deferring an unrelated session's own verify-deploy.sh/run-all.sh call within the marker's own staleness window. Root cause was twofold: (1) a fixed session name raced across concurrent instances of the same suite, and (2) even a PID-unique name could still leak if the suite's own process were SIGKILLed before its EXIT trap fired (run-all.sh's own per-suite timeout kill path). Fixed by replacing the real-repo write entirely with an isolated, path-mirrored run-all.sh fixture copy under the suite's own TMPTARGET -- the same pattern Phase 5's verify-deploy.sh case already used.

That same investigation surfaced the suite's own root cause for failing inside gate 8's real battery despite passing 20/0 standalone: RUN_ALL_NESTED/VERIFY_DEPLOY_NESTED/GATE_MUTEX_HELD are plain exported shell variables that gate 8's own outer run-all.sh sets, silently inherited by any suite it runs as a child -- exempting this suite's own nested/guest-sensitive assertions from the exact guard behavior under test. Fixed with an explicit `unset` at the suite's own top, mirroring test-deploy-verify-wiring.sh's pre-existing 'ANTI-RECURSION INVARIANT' precedent for the same hazard class. The identical, PRE-EXISTING vulnerability was found (via direct reproduction) in test-gate-lock.sh, a suite this task never touches -- recorded as a Reasoned Exclusion and a worthwhile follow-up for a future task, not fixed here (out of this task's own file_scope).

Three residual full-gate-set findings are Reasoned-Excluded in the plan's own Phase 8 section: Gate 27's 3 pre-existing unmigrated subject-resolution call sites (confirmed present before this task began); test-mcp-merge-target.sh's pre-existing, unrelated MCP-merge-target bug (fails standalone, independent of load); and test-gate-lock.sh's own nested-inheritance vulnerability (pre-existing, same root cause class as the one fixed in this task's own new suite, but out of file_scope to fix here).

SKILL.md's context-budget ceiling (gate 20) was breached by this task's own Phase 7 watchdog documentation (29,761 B against a 26,500 B ceiling). Trimmed via three compaction passes (2,267 B reclaimed, landing at 27,494 B) following this file's own established precedent, then closed the residual 994 B via a reviewed, dated ceiling move (26,500 B -> 27,500 B) in orchestrator-context-budget.json, recorded with the same dated-entry convention every prior move in that file already uses.
